references.text: Mary uses the same words as Martha: 'If you had been here, my brother would not have died', which underscores their shared faith in Jesus' power to prevent death.

Some of those standing there repeat Martha's and Mary's question: 'Could not he who opened the eyes of the blind man have kept this man from dying?', showing how Martha's words became a common expression of wonder at Jesus' power.

Jesus' disciples ask about Lazarus' condition with the words, 'Lord, if he sleeps, he will get well', which reflects Martha's belief that Jesus' presence could have brought healing or prevented death.

Martha responds to Jesus' promise of resurrection with the faith that Lazarus will be raised on the last day, showing that her complaint in verse 21 was not doubt in God's power, but grief that Jesus was not present when death occurred.
